questions.question: At 100 million accepted photos per day and 4 MB per original, how much logical original storage arrives each day before copies or derivatives?
options: 400 TB
40 TB
4 PB
25 TB
questions.explanation: 100,000,000 x 4 MB is 400,000,000 MB, or 400 TB using decimal planning units.

questions.question: What must be true before the upload service acknowledges an accepted photo?
options: The original and checksum are durably recorded
Every follower inbox contains the post
Every CDN edge has cached all derivatives
The ranking model has scored the post
questions.explanation: The acknowledgement is a durability promise for the original. Derivatives, moderation, ranking, and feed fan-out continue asynchronously.

questions.question: Which consistency contract best fits publication?
options: The creator gets read-your-writes state while follower feeds converge asynchronously
Every feed and CDN edge updates in one global transaction
The creator may observe an older state after publication succeeds
Feed caches decide whether a post is deleted
questions.explanation: Creator-facing state should be monotonic and authoritative. Feed references can propagate eventually as long as policy and tombstone checks prevent stale exposure.

questions.question: Why use hybrid feed fan-out?
options: It precomputes inboxes for bounded accounts and merges very large accounts at read time
It stores image bytes inside every follower inbox
It removes the need for feed ranking
It makes follower count uniform
questions.explanation: Hybrid fan-out contains write amplification for celebrity accounts while retaining cheap reads for the common case.

questions.question: What is the correct behavior when derivative processors are unavailable?
options: Keep the durable original and queued state, but do not publish an incomplete manifest
Serve the original directly to all followers
Mark the post published and repair it later
Drop the original so the queue cannot grow
questions.explanation: Processor loss should delay publication, not weaken the invariant. The original remains recoverable and jobs can resume or fail over.

questions.question: Why combine immutable versioned CDN URLs with an authorization or tombstone check?
options: Long-lived cached bytes stay correct while removed versions can be denied before every purge completes
It allows derivatives to be overwritten under warm cache keys
It makes moderation optional after publication
It guarantees every edge purges atomically
questions.explanation: Versioned URLs prevent byte confusion, and deny-first policy prevents stale feed or edge state from re-authorizing removed media.

questions.question: Which metric most directly reveals that asynchronous processing is missing the publication promise?
options: Age of the oldest eligible processing job
Total number of stored originals
Average follower count
Number of CDN hostnames
questions.explanation: Queue age measures how long a creator waits for progress. A busy but stable fleet can be healthy, while an aging queue signals a missed freshness target.
